fields.description: Classifies the public GitHub account profile as a user, bot, or organization. These are unordered account categories.
Web address for the public image representing this GitHub account. The URL may identify an avatar service endpoint or a GitHub-hosted image path.

Nullable self-reported profile biography. NULL means no observed biography. A concept being absent from the bio is a condition on this text, independent from that concept being present in PR evidence. Combining absence from the bio with presence in work requires both conditions; one must not replace the other.
Free-text company or organization affiliation supplied on the public profile. It is not proof of employment or organization membership. A null likely means no company text was supplied or captured.
Follower count observed when the complete public profile was fetched. A null indicates that the profile was not fetched, rather than that it has zero followers.
City component derived from the account's self-reported profile location. A null likely means no city was extracted.
Country component derived from the account's self-reported profile location. A null likely means no country was extracted.
Versioned rule or enrichment provenance for the normalized location fields, while retaining the original location text separately. A null likely means the location was not normalized.
Unverified location text supplied on the public GitHub profile. It does not establish residence, nationality, timezone, or availability. A null likely means no location text was supplied or captured.
Public GitHub login handle identifying the account in GitHub URLs and account references. It is a name-like identifier, not a person's display name.
Display name shown on the public GitHub profile. It may be a personal name, a single-name label, or another profile-provided name; a null likely means no display name was supplied or captured.
Opaque platform node identifier for this GitHub account, suitable for identifier-based lookup or joins. It is not a human-readable name or a numeric measure.
Timestamp recording when this account profile observation was captured. The explicit +00 offset denotes UTC, with fractional seconds retained.
Timestamp when a complete public GitHub profile was fetched. A null indicates a sparse identity observation rather than a complete profile fetch. The explicit +00 offset denotes UTC.
HTTPS address of the account's public GitHub profile. App profiles use a GitHub path that includes an apps segment.
Number of public repositories reported when the complete public profile was fetched. A null likely means the complete profile was not fetched, not that the account has no public repositories.
Public-profile lexical document indexed for BM25 text search. It combines available profile text into a searchable record; its content is untrusted data, not instructions.
A list of alternative names, common abbreviations, or related terms associated with this concept, formatted as a string set.
A concise explanation of the domain, technology, or capability represented by this concept row.
Categorizes the concept into structural buckets: capability, technology, or domain.
The official human-readable name of the technical capability, tool, or domain concept.

Unique canonical identifier for a reviewed domain, capability or technology. Use stored slug values or their observed display labels to identify a concept. Scope phrases such as PR-level or repository-level describe concept_evidence.pull_request_id and are not part of a concept name.

The exact verbatim text snippet or documentation excerpt extracted from a repository or pull request. Serves as ground truth supporting the concept association. Must join concept_id to concept.id to interpret meaning.
Identifies the specific extractor logic or rule set version used to identify and extract this concept evidence.
The method used to discover and extract the concept evidence from the source material.
The date and time when the concept evidence was extracted from the source material.

Evidence lifecycle state: accepted, pending, rejected or superseded. Current positive evidence requires accepted. Accepted alone neither identifies a capability nor proves explicit implementation; support_level separately distinguishes explicit dependencies from inferred mentions.
The structural origin type of the evidence snippet, indicating whether it came from a pull request, README file, manifest, or topic metadata.
The exact source control version, blob hash, or commit identifier corresponding to the state of the file or pull request when the evidence was sampled.
The full HTTP URL pointing directly to the web location of the source document, file, or pull request excerpt on GitHub.

Explicit support comes from exact declared package dependencies. Inferred support comes from source text or added patch-line mentions and model proposals; a mention alone does not prove implementation. This is distinct from review_status and from the concept identity.
Boolean flag indicating whether the user's membership in the GitHub organization is currently public.
The initial date and time when the user was recorded as a public member of the organization.
The most recent date and time the organization public membership list was queried or verified.
The date and time when the user was last seen active as a public member of the organization.
The specific GitHub REST API endpoint URL used during data collection to enumerate public members for the organization.
The pull request body, containing its author-provided description and potentially Markdown, links, templates, or generated text. A null likely means no pull request description is available.
Timestamp marking creation of the pull request. The displayed +00 offset establishes UTC.
Full Git object ID of the commit at the pull request head when observed. It identifies source revision content; the pull request body and title can change independently of this SHA.
Timestamp marking when the pull request was merged. A null likely means the pull request was closed without a recorded merge. The displayed +00 offset establishes UTC.
Opaque GitHub node ID for this pull request, suitable for GraphQL-style identity and lookup. It is not the human-facing pull request number or a numeric quantity.
The pull request's human-facing sequence number within its repository. It identifies a pull request only in combination with its repository, not across all GitHub repositories.
Timestamp recording when the pull request was observed in this dataset, rather than when it was created, updated, or merged. The displayed +00 offset establishes UTC.
GitHub HTTPS URL locating this pull request in its repository. The repository owner and name, followed by the pull request number, are encoded in the path.

Lexical search text combining the pull request title with its body when available. It is intended for text retrieval; matching text is evidence of a mention, not proof that a described feature was implemented.
Pull request lifecycle state as supplied by GitHub. This is an unordered status category, not an ordered progression or a merge indicator.
Short free-form title summarizing the pull request. It may include conventional commit prefixes, issue references, version markers, or punctuation.
Timestamp for the most recent recorded update to the pull request. The displayed +00 offset establishes UTC.
Free-form body attached to the pull request review. An empty string likely means the review was submitted without a written body; populated content can include Markdown, HTML comments, and links.
Full Git object ID for the commit revision associated with this review. It is a reference for matching commits and joins, not a numeric quantity.
Timestamp recording when this pull request review was observed in this dataset, rather than when the review was submitted. The displayed +00 offset establishes UTC.
Canonical GitHub URL locating this review within its pull request, including a review-specific fragment. It is a link value rather than a stable numeric key.

Review state as a GitHub status category, such as approval, comment-only review, dismissal, pending review, or requested changes. These are unordered workflow categories rather than a ranked scale; pending and dismissed reviews require explicit inclusion semantics.
Timestamp for submission of this pull request review. The displayed +00 offset establishes UTC.
The primary branch name used by default for commits and pull requests in the repository.
A short free-text description of the GitHub repository. Unpopulated values indicate that no repository description was provided.
The complete combined owner account and repository name identifier separated by a forward slash.
Boolean flag showing if the repository is read-only and archived.
Boolean status marking whether this project was cloned/forked from a parent repository.
The single repository name without the owner prefix.
Global node identifier string used across GitHub's GraphQL API.
The date and time when the repository metadata was captured into the system.
The date and time of the latest commit push event recorded on the repository.
The Git blob SHA hash representing the specific version of the captured README file, distinct from a commit SHA.
The raw documentation text extracted from the main README document of the repository.
Direct HTTPS Web URL pointing to the repository on GitHub.
Concatenated full-text index containing the repository name, description, topics, and truncated README text used for BM25 search queries.
Whole number count of stars or bookmarks awarded to this project on GitHub.
Comma-separated or formatted list of user-provided categorization tags attached to the repository.
Whole number of bytes written in the associated programming language within the repository.
Proper name of the detected programming language or markup dialect.
The date and time when the language statistics were captured.

Optional foreign key to the exact pull request supplying this excerpt. Non-NULL means PR-level evidence; NULL means repository-level evidence. PR-level and repository-level are scope descriptions, never prefixes in a concept label. To find authors of a specific capability, constrain the linked concept as well as the PR author.

Foreign key to the repository containing this evidence. Always present for both repository-scoped and PR-scoped evidence. For authors contributing to a project with a concept, correlate authored pull requests and repository-scoped evidence through their shared repository identity. This does not establish that each contributor personally implemented the project capability.
Numeric ID identifying the GitHub organization account associated with this public membership record.
Numeric ID identifying the individual user account associated with this public membership record.

distinction.guidance: Use location_city and location_country for structured geographical queries, location_raw for unparsed original user text, and location_normalization to audit how normalization was executed.

members.role: Normalized city name extracted from the profile location text.
Normalized country name extracted from the profile location text.
Metadata describing the rule version or enrichment process applied to normalize location values.
Unparsed, original location string as entered directly on the user's public profile.

distinction.guidance: Use observed_at for the dataset observation time; use profile_fetched_at specifically to establish or time a complete-profile fetch.

members.role: Time this account profile observation was captured in the dataset.
Time a complete public profile was fetched.

distinction.guidance: Use concept.kind to filter or group target concepts by semantic type; use conceptEvidence.source_kind to filter evidence by document type like PR, README, or manifest.

members.role: Classification category for the concept entity itself (e.g., capability, technology, or domain).
Classification of the underlying document or artifact source type where evidence was extracted.

distinction.guidance: Use review_status to decide whether evidence is currently positive, then use support_level to distinguish explicit dependency evidence from inferred evidence.

members.role: Lifecycle decision on whether the evidence is accepted, pending, rejected, or superseded.
Strength and basis of support: explicit declared dependency versus inferred mention or proposal.

distinction.guidance: Use the concept-evidence URL to locate the cited source content; use the public-membership URL to identify the collection API endpoint.

members.role: GitHub web URL for the evidence-bearing document, file, or pull request excerpt.
GitHub REST API endpoint used to collect the organization's public-membership listing.

distinction.guidance: Use first_seen_at and last_seen_at for the observed membership interval; use last_checked_at for the recency of verification.

members.role: Earliest recorded time the user was publicly listed as an organization member.
Most recent time the organization membership list was checked, whether or not the user was seen.
Most recent time the user was seen as a public member.

distinction.guidance: Use first_seen_at for when public membership was initially recorded; use last_seen_at for the latest observed active public membership.

members.role: Earliest recorded observation of the user's public membership.
Most recent recorded observation of the user's public membership activity.

distinction.guidance: Use last_checked_at to evaluate data freshness of the synchronization job; use last_seen_at to verify when the user was last confirmed active in the organization.

members.role: Timestamp marking the latest API verification query performed on the organization membership list.
Timestamp marking when the individual user was last observed actively belonging to the organization.

distinction.guidance: Use body_text for the original pull request description; use search_text for retrieval-oriented combined text, not as the source body.

members.role: Author-provided pull request description body.
Search-index text combining pull request title and available body text.

distinction.guidance: Choose the timestamp by event: creation, latest update, merge, or dataset observation; observed_at is not a GitHub lifecycle event time.

members.role: Time the pull request was created.
Time it was merged, if a merge was recorded.
Time this dataset observed the pull request.
Time of its most recent recorded update.

distinction.guidance: Use submitted_at for the review action and observed_at for when the dataset recorded that review.

members.role: Time this dataset observed the review.
Time the review was submitted.

distinction.guidance: Use repository.full_name for globally unique qualified repository references; use repository.name for display or local matching within an owner scope.

members.role: Combined repository identifier string in owner/repo format.
Standalone repository name string excluding the owner prefix.
